exposure: head circumference less than the third percentile
low Apgar index at fifth minute
cohort: 724 infants born between 2007 and 2012 at the University Hospital of Ferrara (Italy) with gestational ages of 33-36 weeks
finding: A considerable number of infants born between 33 and 36 weeks have cranial ultrasonography abnormalities, and the presence of risk factors such as small head circumference, need for respiratory support, low Apgar score, and neurological abnormalities increases the likelihood of these abnormalities.
mod_finding: Statistical analysis revealed no association between cranial ultrasonography abnormalities and mode of delivery.
